label: Individual text/author/source/term/object/local problem
definition: The item addresses a single text, author, source, term, object, or narrowly local problem.
inclusion: A single manuscript reading; one scholar's biography; a single term's etymology. A region, language, period, or named tradition does not by itself raise the level.

label: Explicit tradition, school, genre, or durable historical line
definition: The item explicitly frames a tradition, school, genre, large class, or durable historical line.
inclusion: Comparing texts within one school; genre-level surveys. Requires explicit supra-case framing.
exclusion: A single-object study with no tradition framing (see G1).
examples: survey of a grammatical school's commentaries

label: Broad interregional, civilizational, comparative, or methodological synthesis
definition: The item synthesizes across regions, civilizations, or methodologies.
inclusion: Comparative civilizational arguments; explicit cross-tradition method papers.

label: Not applicable
definition: The item demonstrably does not advance an identifiable scholarly frame at all, so the scale cannot apply.
inclusion: Announcements; bare resource links; greetings; bibliography-only requests. Never forced into G1.
exclusion: Any item making a scholarly claim at any level; items whose applicability is merely undecidable (see unknown).

label: Unknown
definition: The item may well make a scholarly claim, but the evidence is insufficient to decide applicability or level.
inclusion: Missing or unreadable subject/body evidence; ambiguous titles.
exclusion: Any record where a level could be determined; items demonstrably outside the scale (see not_applicable).
